edges.description: Increasing airway bacterial density activates the accessory gene regulator quorum-sensing circuit that controls secreted S. aureus toxins.
Reduced Type 17 immunity impairs bacterial clearance, allowing airway S. aureus burdens to rise to agr-activating density.
edges.source: Influenza Type I IFN Type 17 Suppression

edges.description: Agr activation contributes to the secreted alpha-hemolysin pool that engages ADAM10 on alveolar epithelial cells.
The agr system directly regulates PSM-alpha cytolysins that drive MLKL phosphorylation and neutrophil necroptosis.
Agr-driven cytolysin expression is one part of the larger virulence program that, in PVL-positive strains, produces severe leukocyte injury and necrotizing community-acquired pneumonia.
Alpha-hemolysin/ADAM10 barrier loss contributes to lethal acute lung injury and downstream respiratory failure in severe disease.
Staphylococcal leukocyte lysis is one route by which necrotizing pneumonia presents with peripheral leukopenia.
PVL-positive lung infection is clinically associated with airway bleeding and hemoptysis.
Fatal PVL-positive necrotizing pneumonia has a hemorrhagic pulmonary pattern in systematic review and autopsy material.
PVL-positive severe community-acquired S. aureus pneumonia is associated with greater frequency of septic shock at admission.
Antecedent influenza induces a type I IFN program that suppresses IL-17, IL-22, IL-23, and IL-1β responses needed for staphylococcal clearance.

nodes.description: The S. aureus accessory gene regulator quorum-sensing circuit activates RNAIII-linked virulence expression and upregulates secreted cytolysins, including alpha-hemolysin, PSM-alpha toxins, and PVL.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibiting PSMα-induced neutrophil necroptosis protects mice with MRSA pneumonia by blocking the agr system.
evidence.snippet: Phenol-soluble modulins (PSMs), as major leukocyte lysis toxins of CA-MRSA, are directly regulated by the agr system.

nodes.description: S. aureus alpha-hemolysin engages ADAM10 on alveolar epithelial cells, increases ADAM10 metalloprotease activity, and cleaves E-cadherin to weaken epithelial cell-cell adhesion in the infected lung.

evidence.reference_title: A Staphylococcus aureus pore-forming toxin subverts the activity of ADAM10 to cause lethal infection in mice.
evidence.snippet: Investigation of the molecular mechanism of toxin-receptor function revealed that α-hemolysin upregulates ADAM10 metalloprotease activity in alveolar epithelial cells, resulting in cleavage of the adherens junction protein E-cadherin.

nodes.description: Influenza A co-infection suppresses Type 17 antibacterial defense and attenuates IL-1β/NF-κB activation, creating a permissive post-viral respiratory niche for severe secondary S. aureus pneumonia.

evidence.reference_title: Influenza A inhibits Th17-mediated host defense against bacterial pneumonia in mice.
evidence.snippet: These data indicate a novel mechanism by which influenza A-induced type I IFNs inhibit Th17 immunity and increase susceptibility to secondary bacterial pneumonia.

evidence.reference_title: Influenza A exacerbates Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia by attenuating IL-1β production in mice.
evidence.snippet: Influenza A attenuation of S. aureus induced NF-κB activation, leading to inhibition of IL-1β production and subsequent diminution of Type 17 pathway activation may represent a novel pathway by which influenza predisposes to secondary bacterial infection.

nodes.description: Suvratoxumab is an investigational monoclonal antibody against S. aureus alpha toxin that was tested as single-dose prophylaxis to prevent S. aureus pneumonia in colonized mechanically ventilated ICU patients.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of suvratoxumab for prevention of Staphylococcus aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia (SAATELLITE): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 2 pilot trial.
evidence.snippet: We aimed to evaluate the efficacy of suvratoxumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting the α toxin, in reducing the incidence of S aureus pneumonia in patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who are on mechanical ventilation.

evidence.reference_title: Association between Staphylococcus aureus strains carrying gene for Panton-Valentine leukocidin and highly lethal necrotising pneumonia in young immunocompetent patients.
evidence.snippet: PVL-positive infections were more often marked by: temperature greater than 39 degrees C (p=0.01), heart rate above 140 beats per min (p=0.02), haemoptysis (p=0.005), onset of pleural effusion during hospital stay (p=0.004), and leucopenia (p=0.001).

nodes.description: Antecedent influenza A infection induces type I IFN signaling that suppresses IL-17, IL-22, IL-23, NF-κB, and IL-1β responses, weakening the neutrophilic antibacterial program needed to clear S. aureus from lung.

evidence.reference_title: Influenza A inhibits Th17-mediated host defense against bacterial pneumonia in mice.
evidence.snippet: influenza A coinfection resulted in substantially decreased IL-17, IL-22, and IL-23 production after S. aureus infection.

evidence.reference_title: Factors associated with the outcome of life-threatening necrotizing pneumonia due to community-acquired Staphylococcus aureus in adult and adolescent patients.
evidence.snippet: Logistic regression analysis showed that leucopenia (p = 0.002), influenza-like symptoms or laboratory-confirmed influenza (p = 0.011), and hemoptysis (p = 0.024) were the factors associated with death.

nodes.description: S. aureus enters the lower respiratory tract and proliferates on airway or alveolar surfaces until high local density licenses quorum-sensing-driven virulence-factor production.
Hospital-acquired or nosocomial MRSA pneumonia is treated with active antibiotics such as linezolid or vancomycin, which lower the viable bacterial burden.

evidence.reference_title: A 600 mg of fixed-dose linezolid in renally impaired patients versus 15 mg/kg intermittent dose-optimized vancomycin in renally non-impaired patients: A single centre retrospective analysis for adult patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
evidence.snippet: Both linezolid and vancomycin are approved by USFDA and IDSA guidelines for the management of nosocomial pneumonia due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in clinical practice.

nodes.description: Methicillin-susceptible S. aureus pneumonia is treated with an active anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam such as cefazolin, nafcillin, or oxacillin once MSSA is established.

evidence.reference_title: Cefazolin vs. antistaphylococcal penicillins for the treatment of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: There is debate on whether cefazolin or antistaphylococcal penicillins should be the first-line treatment for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia.

nodes.description: Agr-regulated PSM-alpha cytolysins trigger MLKL phosphorylation and necroptosis in recruited neutrophils, releasing neutrophil contents and reducing cellular bacterial clearance.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibiting PSMα-induced neutrophil necroptosis protects mice with MRSA pneumonia by blocking the agr system.
evidence.snippet: PSMα1, 2, and 3 significantly induced neutrophil necroptosis by activating mixed lineage kinase-like protein (MLKL) phosphorylation and increasing lactate dehydrogenase release.

nodes.description: PVL-positive S. aureus strains carry LukS-PV/LukF-PV leukocidin and are clinically associated with rapidly progressive hemorrhagic necrotizing pneumonia, leukopenia, airway bleeding, septic shock, and increased mortality.

evidence.reference_title: Prognostic factors of severe community-acquired staphylococcal pneumonia in France.
evidence.snippet: Thus, PVL positivity was a risk factor of mortality independent of other baseline factors.

evidence.reference_title: Fatal septic shock due to PVL-positive Staphylococcus aureus necrotizing pneumonia: autopsy findings and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Most cases were characterized by rapid clinical deterioration, frequent septic shock, and hemoptysis or pulmonary hemorrhage.

evidence.reference_title: Fatal septic shock due to PVL-positive Staphylococcus aureus necrotizing pneumonia: autopsy findings and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: PVL-positive S. aureus pneumonia represents a rare but highly aggressive infection that may rapidly progress to respiratory failure and death.

evidence.reference_title: Prognostic factors of severe community-acquired staphylococcal pneumonia in France.
evidence.snippet: In addition, PVL-positive CAP patients were more likely to present with septic shock, leukopenia, elevated blood lactate and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) severity score, and to require extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

nodes.description: Protein-synthesis inhibitors such as linezolid or clindamycin are used when toxin suppression is desired in necrotizing community-associated MRSA pneumonia.

evidence.reference_title: Factors associated with the outcome of life-threatening necrotizing pneumonia due to community-acquired Staphylococcus aureus in adult and adolescent patients.
evidence.snippet: Antibiotic therapies inhibiting toxin production were associated with an improved outcome in these cases (p = 0.007).

evidence.reference_title: Pulmonary infections and community associated methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus: a dangerous mix?
evidence.snippet: Linezolid and clindamycin have also been used in the treatment of CA-MRSA pneumonia and ongoing research is looking for alternative antimicrobials.
